lessons.title: Cold Flow Fundamentals
lessons.content: A Flow is cold - the producer block doesn't run until a collector calls collect(). Each new collector re-runs the whole producer independently, unlike a hot stream. Real scenario: a Flow<List<Lesson>> backed by Room's @Query - each screen observing it gets its own independent stream, and Room automatically re-emits whenever the underlying table changes, keeping UI in sync without manual refresh calls.

lessons.title: Key Operators: debounce, distinctUntilChanged, flatMapLatest
lessons.content: debounce waits for a pause in emissions before emitting the latest value - essential for search-as-you-type so you don't fire an API call per keystroke. distinctUntilChanged skips consecutive duplicate emissions, preventing unnecessary recompositions. flatMapLatest cancels the previous inner flow when a new value arrives - critical for search, where you want to cancel an in-flight query the moment the user types another character.

codeSnippets.code:
val searchResults = searchQuery
    .debounce(300)
    .distinctUntilChanged()
    .flatMapLatest { query ->
        if (query.isBlank()) flowOf(emptyList())
        else repository.search(query) // previous search auto-cancelled
    }
    .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList())

lessons.title: StateFlow vs SharedFlow vs Channel
lessons.content: StateFlow always holds a current value, replays it to new collectors, and conflates rapid updates (only the latest value matters) - perfect for UI state. SharedFlow is more flexible: configurable replay count and no requirement to hold an initial value - good for one-time events like navigation or snackbar triggers, though a common mistake is using SharedFlow(replay=0) but forgetting that if no collector is active when the event fires, it's lost. Channel is for single-consumer, point-to-point communication (like a work queue) rather than broadcast to multiple observers.
